_comment: Modular watch-guide database for the txtempus web UI. To add a watch, copy an entry and edit it -- no code change needed. Installed to /etc/txtempus-watches.json (which you can edit on the device). Fields: brand, model, stations (which signals the watch can receive, using txtempus names DCF77/WWVB/MSF/JJY40/JJY60/BPC), sync_times (when it auto-receives, in the WATCH's own local time, HH:MM), setup (short how-to steps), notes.

setup: Set the watch's home city to a city in the region of the station you are broadcasting (the U680 uses the home city to choose which signal to seek: EUR=DCF77, USA=WWVB, JPN=JJY, CHN=BPC). It does not receive MSF.
Make sure the time-zone / DST setting on the watch matches what txtempus is sending (see the 'Will set watch to' line above).
Leave automatic reception ON; the watch tries to receive overnight (around 2-4 AM watch time).
To force a reception now: pull the crown to the receive position and trigger a manual receive per the manual, then rest the watch on/next to the antenna loop for a few minutes.
watches.notes: Multi-band Eco-Drive. The R (receive) hand shows L (received) or N/H (not received). Keep the watch within a few cm of the coil; too close can also fail.

setup: Set the Home City to a city served by the station you are broadcasting (this selects which signal it listens for).
Enable Auto Receive; the watch attempts reception several times overnight.
For an immediate sync, hold the dedicated receive button (often the lower-left) until it starts receiving, with the 12 o'clock side near the coil.
Check the DST (summer time) setting is Auto or matches the broadcast.
watches.notes: Multi-Band 6 supports all five world stations plus BPC. Signal level shows on the dial after a manual receive.

setup: Most Mega models receive automatically at night; place the watch near the coil overnight.
If the model has a manual send/receive function, trigger it and hold the watch by the coil.
watches.notes: The original watch this project was built for. No band/timezone selection -- it just decodes DCF77.

setup: Insert the battery near the coil, or leave the clock beside the coil overnight -- many clocks attempt reception right after power-on and hourly at night.
Make sure the clock's manual time-zone offset (if any) matches the broadcast.
watches.notes: Most inexpensive 'radio controlled' clocks sold in Europe are DCF77.
